courses.title: Prompt Airlines CTF
courses.description: Wiz CTF with five chat-only challenges against an airline customer-service chatbot: find its identifier, extract its full instructions, get it to disclose hidden coupon codes, get past a third-party AI membership check, and book a free flight. No coding is needed, and an 'Under the Hood' panel shows what happens behind the chat. It has little explanatory content.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N3 Weak 5%; N12 Weak 4%; R3.1 Partial 33% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Chatbot challenges expose prompt-driven authentication bypass without teaching a secure authorisation design. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

Reviewed syllabus: Self-hosted LangChain ReAct banking-chatbot agent (Streamlit, OpenAI/HF/Ollama) with two flags: make the agent fetch another user's transactions, and use Thought/Action/Observation injection to push a UNION SQL injection through its tool and extract a password. courses.title: Damn Vulnerable MCP Server (10 challenges)
courses.description: Dockerised set of 10 deliberately vulnerable MCP servers, used from an MCP client such as Cline. The challenges are basic and indirect prompt injection, tool poisoning, excessive permission scope, rug pull, tool shadowing, token theft, code execution, command injection and a chained multi-vector attack. It has objectives per challenge and a solutions guide but no taught material or mitigation guidance.

audit.priorFit: The best free lab in this batch for MCP-specific attack classes (tool poisoning, rug pull, shadowing). courses.title: Red teaming LLM agents (docs)
courses.description: A Promptfoo documentation guide that maps agent attack classes to the tool's red-team plugins and strategies: privilege escalation (RBAC/BOLA/BFLA), context poisoning and exfiltration, memory poisoning, multi-stage chains, tool/API manipulation, objective hijacking and prompt leak. It gives example YAML configs for black-box, component-level and trace-based testing, and shows how to turn findings into trajectory-assertion regression tests. It is a reading and lab guide for engineers who build a test harness, not a course.

courses.title: AI Capabilities and Limitations
courses.description: Foundation AI literacy focused on model limitations, with L1 context, discernment and memory practice. 13 lessons, one quiz and a completion badge. No prerequisites. Public lessons cover model training, prediction, knowledge, context and instruction following, with exercises on personal work tasks. Companion to AI Fluency; either course may be taken first.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: V12 review: N2 19% Weak; N3 76% Partial (prompt-injection core gap); N6 54% Partial. Current results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: 31 Oct 2026: Foundation (N3), with L1 practice (N6); generic and transferable, not specialist cyber or Claude product training. Published learning estimate 3.5h. Public lessons/exercises inspected; not a completion claim. Prompt injection, bank rules and cyber threats still need other teaching. Exceeds the 2h Foundation course budget. Supersedes the historical V8 audit for this course.

courses.title: Teaching AI Fluency
courses.description: A course for faculty and instructional designers, built with professors from University College Cork and Ringling College, on teaching and assessing the 4D AI Fluency framework. It covers the Delegation-Diligence and Description-Discernment loops, outcome-, process- and reflection-based assessment, assignment design, and applying discipline expertise. It is mostly readings plus one quiz, and assumes learners have done AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N6 Partial 33%; N14 Weak 5% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Teaching/assessment of human AI fluency may support internal trainers. Assessing students is not N9/N11 evaluation of AI systems. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: AI Systems Security Specialist learning path + eAIS certification
courses.cost: Subscription (INE Premium USD 799/yr includes one exam voucher)
courses.description: A vendor-neutral learning path with hands-on labs (INE Premium) and an auto-graded, scenario-based exam. Its five domains are abuse and exploitation 25%, secure design and controls 30%, foundations 15%, testing 20% and safe operational use 10%. The modules cover AI systems, embeddings/RAG security, prompt injection and jailbreaks, tool and agentic-workflow abuse, defensive controls, secure integrations, human-in-the-loop automation, telemetry and AI security testing. Course and lab lists are visible only inside the platform, so only the module names and published topic lists were seen.

courses.title: CompTIA SecAI+ preparation path (3 courses + practice exam)
courses.description: Four video courses by Christopher Rees, one per SecAI+ exam domain: Basic AI Concepts (2h13), Securing AI Systems (3h22), AI-assisted Security (1h55) and AI Governance, Risk and Compliance (1h56, added 5 Oct 2026). They cover threat-modelling resources (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS), guardrails and gateway controls, access control including agent access, data protection, monitoring, a full AI attack catalogue, AI tools including MCP, AI-enabled attacks including deepfakes, security automation with agents, and governance and compliance (EU AI Act, ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF). It is lecture-only with scenario clips and no labs. Clip titles for the Basic Concepts course were not visible.

courses.title: LDR553: Cyber Incident Management (GIAC GCIL)
courses.description: SANS incident-management leadership course with 27 labs and a capstone, leading to GIAC GCIL. AI content: building a GPT as a team member (Lab 1.5), GenAI for briefs and comms checks, Section 4 'agentic AI governance during incidents', which introduces the CORDS framework (Confirm, Own, Restrain, Document, Sanction) with graduated restraint from pausing a queue to termination and evidence preservation before reset, and Section 5 AI/LLM risk plus Lab 5.1 'Managing an Agent Incident'. The rest is classic incident management (comms, BEC, cloud, ransomware).

courses.title: SEC450: AI-Enabled Security Operations (GIAC GSOC)
courses.description: Intermediate SOC analyst course with 19 labs and a capstone, leading to GIAC GSOC, rebuilt around AI. AI labs: AI Prompting for SOC Analysts, AI Output Verification, Manual and Agentic Alert Enrichment, AI-Enabled Analysis Tools, an AI-powered phishing-triage workflow, Agent-Controlled Automation, an AI-Assisted Workflow Risk Assessment and building a custom SOC utility with AI. Topics include agentic concepts, agent configuration and context, prompt-injection risk, approval gates, audit trails, least privilege, and separating facts from AI inferences. About half the course is classic SOC content (network, telemetry, email, YARA-X, Sigma).

courses.title: Governing AI Agents
courses.cost: Free access advertised at review; Pro graded work/accomplishment; external service costs may apply
courses.description: Short beginner course built with Databricks: the four pillars of agent governance (lifecycle, risk, security, observability), giving an agent its own identity, least-privilege data access through Unity Catalog, anonymised views and PII masking on an HR dataset, and logging, evaluating and deploying the agent with MLflow tracing. It has three video-walkthrough labs, no code examples, and a graded quiz for Pro users. It is heavily Databricks-specific.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N2 Weak 19%; N4 Weak 11%; N7 Weak 7%; N9 Weak 7%; N10 Weak 4%; N11 Weak 6%; N12 Weak 22%; R9.1 Weak 14% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Databricks walkthroughs teach distinct identity, least-privilege data access and tracing. Product-specific demonstrations are partial skills coverage, not complete bank governance. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit. V10 recheck (2026-10-18): Rechecked Databricks identity, least-privilege views, PII masking and MLflow tracing walkthroughs. Existing scores remain appropriate; refresh access metadata and retain the limitation that product demonstrations do not establish full bank governance.

Reviewed syllabus: Short beginner course built with Databricks: the four pillars of agent governance (lifecycle, risk, security, observability), giving an agent its own identity, least-privilege data access through Unity Catalog, anonymised views and PII masking on an HR dataset, and logging, evaluating and deploying the agent with MLflow tracing. courses.title: Prepare an enterprise governance strategy for AI agents
courses.description: A short beginner Microsoft Learn module (9 units) for leaders and administrators. It covers governance through identity (per-agent Entra Agent ID), containment (OS-level execution containers, workload isolation) and management (policies that allow, block or elevate actions, plus audit). It shows matching controls to agent risk through a three-agent example, a control-plane versus execution-layer model, and an Audit-Define-Refresh strategy (inventory and owners, per-agent identity and sponsor requirements). It ends with a pitch for Windows 11 Pro and Copilot+ PCs and has a knowledge check only.

N5.8.evidence: V11 reassessment (18 October 2026). Security/privacy risks, safety constraints or controls are named in the retained public syllabus, but a coherent explanation of the revised security-risk overview is not established. Reviewed syllabus: A short beginner Microsoft Learn module (9 units) for leaders and administrators. It covers governance through identity (per-agent Entra Agent ID), containment (OS-level execution containers, workload isolation) and management (policies that allow, block or elevate actions, plus audit). It shows matching controls to agent risk through a three-agent example, a control-plane versus execution-layer model, and an Audit-Define-Refresh strategy (inventory and owners, per-agent identity and sponsor requirements). It ends with a pitch for Windows 11 Pro and Copilot+ PCs and has a knowledge check only.

courses.title: AI security fundamentals
courses.description: Beginner Microsoft Learn path of three text modules: AI-specific attacks (jailbreak, prompt injection, model manipulation, data exfiltration, overreliance) against a three-layer AI architecture; AI security controls (open-source library review, content filters, data security, metaprompts, grounding, app security, monitoring); and an introduction to AI red teaming. Each module ends with a knowledge check; no labs. Not agent-specific.

Reviewed syllabus: Beginner Microsoft Learn path of three text modules: AI-specific attacks (jailbreak, prompt injection, model manipulation, data exfiltration, overreliance) against a three-layer AI architecture; AI security controls (open-source library review, content filters, data security, metaprompts, grounding, app security, monitoring); and an introduction to AI red teaming. Each module ends with a knowledge check; no labs. Not agent-specific.

courses.title: Agentic AI maturity model, pillar 3: AI governance and security
courses.description: Microsoft guidance page describing a five-level (100-500) maturity model for governing and securing agents built on Copilot Studio and Foundry: agent ownership, a central registry, classification by purpose, criticality and autonomy, tiered and zoned governance, an AI Council, audit logging and AI-specific incident response. It adds governance anti-patterns and a 'Responsible AI risk radar' exercise (impact x likelihood across six principles). Reading only, no exercises beyond the worked risk-radar example; regulation is mentioned only generically (NIST AI RMF).
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N2 Weak 5%; N7 Weak 7%; N11 Weak 6%; N12 Weak 4%; N13 Partial 44%; N14 Partial 33%; R4.1 Weak 11%; R6.1 Weak 17% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Maturity guidance includes ownership, registry and telemetry; a maturity checklist is not a control-testing course. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: Security Engineering for Agentic AI Systems
courses.description: Packt course based on Anand Rao Nednur's book covering agent goal integrity, tool security and sandboxing, non-human identity and per-action authorisation, agentic supply chain (MCP/tool descriptor attacks, AIBOM), code execution safety, memory poisoning, multi-agent protocol security, cascading failures, human-agent trust, rogue agents and kill switches, ending in a capstone to design and threat-model a secure agent. Each module has short 'lab' videos (3-7 min, which look like walkthroughs rather than graded hands-on labs) and a 16-min graded quiz; the capstone is an assignment. No course reviews yet; intermediate per Coursera, depth Expert.

courses.title: Balancing speed and safety: a control framework for AI coding agents
courses.description: AWS Security Blog post (level 300) setting out seven risks of AI coding agents (prompt injection, permissive configs, uncontrolled change, supply chain, external access via MCP, incorrect code, scope creep) and a two-pillar control framework: author-time (steering documents, reviewed specs, allow-listed least-privilege MCP tools, IDE scanning, hooks) and build-time (layered scanning, quality gates, AI-assisted review by a different model, risk-scaled human review). It distinguishes deterministic, non-deterministic and human controls and warns about consent fatigue. Reading only, with AWS/Kiro implementation notes.

Reviewed syllabus: AWS Security Blog post (level 300) setting out seven risks of AI coding agents (prompt injection, permissive configs, uncontrolled change, supply chain, external access via MCP, incorrect code, scope creep) and a two-pillar control framework: author-time (steering documents, reviewed specs, allow-listed least-privilege MCP tools, IDE scanning, hooks) and build-time (layered scanning, quality gates, AI-assisted review by a different model, risk-scaled human review). courses.title: Agentic Skills Top 10 (AST10) v1.0
courses.description: OWASP incubator project listing the ten main risks of agent Skills (malicious skills, supply chain compromise, over-privileged skills, insecure metadata, untrusted external instructions, weak isolation, update drift, poor scanning, no governance, cross-platform reuse), mapped to CSA MAESTRO, with mitigations: verified publishers, semantic scanning at publish and install, signing and content hashes, minimal permission manifests, sandboxed execution, inventories and approval workflows. Reading only; still a draft under public review. Per-risk detail pages were not opened.

courses.title: Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A): AI Governance & Compliance
courses.description: Non-technical lecture course for governance, risk and compliance staff on the A2A protocol (agent cards, tasks, opacity), how it differs from MCP, the governance risks of agent-to-agent delegation (identity, traceability, observability, data in transit) and its mapping to the EU AI Act, ISO 42001 and NIST AI RMF, with vendor questions, a usage-policy template and a readiness checklist. Demos and a case study; no labs. Bestseller, 1,453 ratings.

courses.title: AI Agent Governance & Risk Management
courses.description: Non-technical course on governing agents that act in real systems: agent inventory, permissions and autonomy levels, risk scoring by impact and likelihood into tiers, behavioural boundaries, human-in-the-loop vs human-in-command, logging and escalation, a governance operating model, production monitoring, global/EU/Chinese AI regulation and high-risk scenarios. One practice quiz and a final workshop to build a 30-day governance plan for one agent. Two final sections were collapsed on the page.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N2 Weak 10%; N7 Weak 20%; N12 Weak 4%; N13 Partial 50%; N14 Weak 29%; R4.1 Weak 11%; R5.1 Weak 11% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Agent inventory, permission boundaries, monitoring and risk-tiered autonomy are explicit. Governance planning is not operational sign-off. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: AI Agent Security: AI Security
courses.description: Eden Marco's hands-on course: learners deploy a vulnerable web-based help-desk agent on Google Cloud, then exploit and fix it: excessive agency and blast radius, broken access control fixed with RBAC on tool calls, data exfiltration via indirect prompt injection (traced in LangSmith) fixed with tool validation and data boundaries, and memory poisoning. A short opening section covers agentic coding security and treating Skills and MCP servers as code execution. No graded quizzes; practice is exploit/fix along with the instructor.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N2 Weak 10%; N3 Weak 24%; N4 Weak 14%; N5 Weak 11%; N7 Weak 13%; N8 Weak 27%; N9 Weak 7%; N12 Partial 44%; R3.1 Partial 50%; R5.1 Weak 11% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Exploit/fix walkthrough uses LangSmith traces and RBAC on tool calls; Skills/MCP are treated as code execution. No full supervisor cycle or general evaluation suite. The prompt-hardening lecture synopsis explicitly explains why non-deterministic models cannot provide a guaranteed security boundary. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: AI Agents and Agentic AI for Leaders
courses.description: Short non-technical course for business leaders: what agents are (observe-think-act loop), business use cases and when not to use agents, designing with guardrails and human oversight, a hallucination demo in Gemini, metrics and KPIs, pilot vs scaling, risks, ethics and governance, and a 90-day roadmap. Lectures of 3-7 minutes with four knowledge-check quizzes; no exercises. Not cyber-specific.

courses.description: A short video course by Alex Genadinik that explains how hallucinations differ from ordinary errors and bad reasoning. courses.title: AI Ethics & Decision Making, Research Insights & Strategies
courses.description: A non-technical ethics course that uses moral philosophy (the trolley problem, moral foundations, System 1 and 2 thinking) and case studies of AI going wrong (healthcare AI, COMPAS, the Uber self-driving crash, Facebook ad discrimination) to teach ethical decision-making and fixing biased training data. It ends with tips on generative AI content. There are recap quizzes and short practice exercises.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N3 Weak 5% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Human cognitive shortcuts and ethical decision examples provide limited automation-bias awareness; general fairness is not sycophancy. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: AI Ethics & Governance for Corporates: Compliance Mastery
courses.description: A long, case-led governance course covering 2023-2025 AI incidents, ethics principles, the global regulatory map, a full EU AI Act walkthrough, the NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, building a governance framework (policies, inventory and risk register, controls, vendor management, metrics), AI risk assessment, bias testing, drift monitoring and change management. Assessment is by end-of-section quizzes, with 50+ downloadable templates. There are no labs. Two final sections were collapsed on the page.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N3 Weak 14%; N4 Partial 38%; N11 Weak 11%; N13 Partial 50%; N14 Weak 5% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Governance outline explicitly includes drift monitoring and change management; no agent supervision or validated judge method. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: AI Ethics & Responsible Use of AI – A Beginner’s Guide
courses.description: A beginner course narrated by a text-to-speech voice. It walks through four pillars of responsible AI with an example for each, AI bias, four 'Modern Risks' lectures (per the description: hallucinations, misinformation, deepfakes, data leaks), when to use and not use AI, and a S.A.F.E. checklist. There are no quizzes or exercises, only a template and a reading list.

courses.title: AI Ethics 101: AI Ethics & Responsible AI for AI Governance
courses.description: A non-technical course mixing generative AI basics, prompt engineering essentials (prompt structure, good versus bad prompts) and 'ethical prompting' (bias-detection prompts, accuracy and verification prompts, prompts for high-stakes areas), plus an overview of AI ethics principles and common risks. It has four quizzes and an AI 'coach'. Three of the 13 sections were collapsed on the page.

courses.title: AI Ethics and Guardrails for People Managers
courses.description: A manager-focused course on setting team-level AI guardrails. It covers four risk zones (privacy, bias, accountability, transparency), a three-tier task framework (approved, needs review, off-limits), turning company AI policy into task-level boundaries, a checklist for ambiguous cases, team conversations, and containing and escalating an AI incident in the first hour. It includes written activities that produce a boundary list, a script and a 30-day plan.

Security/privacy risks, safety constraints or controls are named in the retained public syllabus, but a coherent explanation of the revised security-risk overview is not established. Reviewed syllabus: A compliance-style responsible-use module for all employees. It covers five ethical AI principles, a three-question risk check, protecting privacy when using ChatGPT, disclosing AI-assisted work, the EU AI Act for employees, bias, GDPR and CCPA, working within a company AI governance framework, and a lecture on governing AI agents that act on your behalf. Short scenarios (The Oversharing Colleague, The Biased Shortlist, The Unapproved Tool) and a capstone action plan are included. It is very widely used (28,800 students).

courses.title: AI for CXOs & Managers : Governance, ISO 42001, Claude
courses.description: An executive overview of predictive, generative and agentic AI (including agents versus agentic AI and multi-LLM strategy), AI governance through an ISO 42001 lens (policy-to-behaviour, lifecycle, risk management, maturity), and Claude features (Skills, connectors, MCP, Claude Code, multi-agent orchestration). Use cases in finance, operations and HR, and vibe-coding demos, are included. Six of the 16 sections were collapsed on the page, and the only practice is case-study assignments.

courses.title: AI for Helping Professions: Safety & Ethics
courses.description: A course by a chartered psychologist and software engineer for therapists, coaches and other client-facing professionals. It covers hands-on use of Claude (documents, choosing a model, temporary chats, voice), prompting with roles and context, how LLMs work (memory, web search), public versus enterprise versus local LLMs, anonymising client documents, hallucinations, echo chambers, bias, deskilling, copyright, checking sources and reviewing output, and installing and using Ollama locally. It has four quizzes, a try-it exercise and the Ollama set-up.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N2 Partial 38%; N3 Partial 33%; N4 Partial 44%; N6 Partial 58%; N14 Weak 5% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.

courses.title: AI Fundamentals 2026: Safe AI Skills for Work
courses.description: Broad workplace AI-literacy course: how LLMs work and fail (hallucination, confident errors), what agents are with ChatGPT/Claude agent demos, a long AI safety section (consumer vs enterprise tools, sensitive data, IP, human-in-the-loop, verification, EU AI Act), structured prompting, custom GPTs/Copilot agents, vibe coding, no-code automation (n8n) and Gemini/Office. 131 lectures with quizzes and nine short exercises (e.g. 'Don't Leak Sensitive Data', 'Prompt Before and After Challenge', 'Create Your First AI Agent'); three of 13 sections were not visible.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N2 Partial 48%; N3 Partial 33%; N4 Partial 50%; N6 Partial 50%; N7 Weak 13% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Consumer-agent demos introduce boundaries and review; no bank action-class supervision or incident drill. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

Security/privacy risks, safety constraints or controls are named in the retained public syllabus, but a coherent explanation of the revised security-risk overview is not established. Reviewed syllabus: Broad workplace AI-literacy course: how LLMs work and fail (hallucination, confident errors), what agents are with ChatGPT/Claude agent demos, a long AI safety section (consumer vs enterprise tools, sensitive data, IP, human-in-the-loop, verification, EU AI Act), structured prompting, custom GPTs/Copilot agents, vibe coding, no-code automation (n8n) and Gemini/Office. 131 lectures with quizzes and nine short exercises (e.g. 'Don't Leak Sensitive Data', 'Prompt Before and After Challenge', 'Create Your First AI Agent'); three of 13 sections were not visible.

courses.title: AI fundamentals for Beginners - Learn LLM, Agentic AI, MCP
courses.description: Hands-on beginner-to-builder course (Himanshu Rana): local models with Ollama, LLM basics (tokens, context window, sampling), prompt patterns (few-shot, CoT, ReAct), building and deploying an AIOps agent with tools on AWS Bedrock AgentCore (IAM scoping, observability), RAG and agentic RAG in Langflow, MCP fundamentals and building an MCP server, and Claude/Claude Code including using and creating Skills. Project-based, no quizzes; requires basic Python/AWS.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N2 Partial 57%; N3 Weak 19%; N4 Weak 6%; N6 Weak 25%; N7 Weak 13%; N8 Weak 20%; N10 Partial 38%; N12 Weak 19% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): AIOps AgentCore project includes IAM scoping and observability. v7's statement of no security/supervision content was too absolute; coverage remains partial. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: AI Governance Fundamentals: Framework, Templates & Sprint
courses.description: Practical starter course (Ritesh Vajariya) built around a fictional 200-person firm: why governance, the four-part framework (AI inventory, seven-category risk scoring, acceptable-use policy, RACI accountability), regulation (EU AI Act, US state/federal, regulated industries), audit evidence, maturity model and a 30-day governance sprint. Includes Excel/Word templates, two assignments with instructor solutions, AI role plays (CEO briefing, shadow AI) and a final quiz.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N4 Weak 22%; N13 Partial 50%; N14 Weak 14% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): RACI and a 30-day governance sprint support change planning; accountability is generic AI rather than per-agent. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: AI Governance Professional (AIGP) 2026 Complete Training
courses.description: Exam-prep course (Saahil Gupta) following the 2026 IAPP AIGP body of knowledge: AI definitions, harms and risks, lifecycle, an introduction to agentic AI and architectures, governance infrastructure and third-party risk, GDPR and other laws, the EU AI Act in depth plus US, Italian, Korean and Vietnamese laws, OECD, NIST AI RMF and ISO 22989/42001/42005, and governing development and deployment. 74 lectures with practice quizzes, two practice tests, five case studies and 400+ pages of notes.

courses.title: AI Governance: Build a Managed AI System
courses.description: Executive-oriented governance course (Thalita Milan, Anton Voroniuk) on bringing shadow AI under management: AI audit and usage report, data classification and risk levels, impact-likelihood risk map, allowed/restricted/prohibited uses, executive rules, AI owner and governance structure, tool approval process, incident management and a CEO dashboard. 28 short lectures; deliverables described but no labs or quizzes.

courses.title: AI Governance: The Fundamentals of AI Governance
courses.description: Popular no-code governance course (Data Universe): AI lifecycle governance, data governance (licensing, bias, copyright for GenAI), inherent risks including security, agentic AI and third-party model dependencies, a long regulation section (EU AI Act and GPAI, US, China, ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, Council of Europe), roles and stakeholders, quick implementation, sector use cases including finance, and closing lectures on governing AI agents and the AI literacy obligation. 52 lectures with a practice test, a sign-off scenario and downloadable templates (inventory, risk matrix, policy, model documentation); three sections not visible.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N4 Partial 44%; N11 Weak 11%; N13 Partial 44%; N14 Weak 5% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.

courses.title: AI Leader: Generative AI & Agentic AI for Leaders & Founders
courses.description: An executive briefing by Ed Donner in three sections (strategist, decision maker, leader): core LLM terms, frontier vs open-source model choice, RAG and fine-tuning, agents vs workflows, AI strategy and decision frameworks, project ideation, AI teams, roadmaps, adoption and ROI. Lectures only; no quizzes, exercises or hands-on use.

courses.title: AI Literacy | The EU Artificial Intelligence Act Article 4
courses.description: An all-employee AI literacy course built around EU AI Act Article 4: what AI is, AI in workflows and high-risk use cases, safe-use do's and don'ts (what not to enter, company policy, GDPR/CCPA-aware prompting), bias and hallucination with human review, global regulation (EU AI Act, US orders, India DPDP), productivity use and regulatory sandboxes. Video lectures with one section quiz and a closing scenarios practice test.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N3 Weak 24%; N4 Partial 44%; N6 Partial 33%; N13 Weak 6% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Regulatory overview introduces compliance context; no full control mapping for GRC specialists. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: AI Literacy Basics: Apply, Understand and Use AI Responsibly
courses.description: A non-technical AI literacy and ethics course: what AI is, use cases, human-AI collaboration and avoiding blind dependence, detecting bias/errors/hallucinations, privacy and misinformation, responsible-AI principles, the EU AI Act and internal AI policy. Short lectures, two practice tests, a guided ethical-dilemma simulation, a compliance scenario and downloadable policy templates and checklists.

courses.title: AI Literacy Basics: Applying Generative AI in the Workplace
courses.description: A five-hour beginner course by Nicolle Merrill: how generative AI and LLMs work, multimodal models, prompting and adding data to prompts, data privacy, demos across content, documents, data analysis and vibe coding, limitations, hallucination and bias, prompt templates and custom GPTs, and a recent section on AI agents (agents vs assistants, ChatGPT and Claude Cowork agent demos, managing agents). Many hands-on activities, no quizzes or graded labs.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N1 Partial 44%; N2 Partial 43%; N3 Weak 14%; N4 Weak 22%; N6 Partial 42%; N7 Weak 13%; N14 Weak 5% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Agent-management lesson and workflow outcomes introduce supervision/design without operational practice. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: AI Literacy for the Modern Workplace (Generative AI Upskill)
courses.description: A compact course by Anthony Alicea: how LLMs are trained and run (determinism, inference, context), prompt anatomy and workplace uses with practice, a risk section on hallucinations, privacy, drift, over-reliance, confirmation bias, sycophancy and hidden instructions (prompt injection), and human-AI collaboration with a risk-value decision framework. Includes practice items, assignments and a Udemy role-play exercise; no quizzes.

courses.title: AI Red Teaming & LLM Hacking - A Practical Guide with Labs
courses.description: Short hands-on course built on Microsoft's AI Red Teaming Playground labs (Docker + Azure OpenAI): direct prompt injection, metaprompt extraction, multi-turn Crescendo jailbreaks and guardrail bypass, and indirect prompt injection via poisoned web content, through six labs and a challenge, with a 5-minute mitigations lecture and mapping to the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs. Bonus lectures on running uncensored local models and 'hacking with Gemini CLI'.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N2 Weak 5%; N3 Weak 14%; N5 Weak 17%; N12 Weak 7%; R3.1 Partial 50% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Crescendo lab demonstrates active-guardrail bypass. Local-model setup is for a lab, not enterprise hosting design. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: AI Safety, AI Security, and Responsible AI at Work
courses.description: Non-technical lecture course distinguishing AI safety, security, privacy and governance, covering common AI risks, protecting data in prompts (placeholders, minimum context), accuracy and verification with a 'Draft, Review, Verify, Approve' workflow, security threats (prompt injection, phishing, deepfakes, risky integrations), and a 7-minute lecture on agents and automation risk. One quiz; ends with a personal toolkit and 6-part action plan.

courses.title: AI Security
courses.description: Christopher Nett's course for SOC, CTI and security engineers: Azure and Microsoft security basics, GenAI fundamentals, a long Microsoft Security Copilot block (2h36m), demos using ChatGPT for SOC, CTI, vulnerability management and AppSec, then OWASP Top 10 for LLMs with demos (PortSwigger vulnerable LLM lab), other GenAI risks, a GenAI threat-modelling method, MITRE ATT&CK and ATLAS (with case studies) and Defender CSPM for AI. Demo-led, with learner lab accounts; no quizzes.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N1 Partial 44%; N2 Weak 10%; N3 Weak 24%; N4 Partial 33%; N5 Weak 22%; N6 Weak 21%; N8 Weak 7%; N12 Weak 19%; R3.1 Partial 67% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Copilot extension/plugin walkthrough introduces tool connectivity, without a complete MCP safe-use or vetting method. Overreliance is explicitly listed among GenAI threat vectors, but the public synopsis does not establish a complete treatment of human automation bias. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: AI Security Awareness: Toward Safe AI Use at Work and Life!
courses.description: Long lecture course (Cyvitrix) on safe workplace AI use: what never to put into AI tools, confidentiality and privacy, approved vs public tools, safe prompting for many tasks and functions (including cybersecurity and GRC), hallucination, verification, bias, copyright, prompt injection, human review and disclosure, AI use policy and a decision tree, incident reporting, and six case studies. No labs or quizzes listed; ends with a capstone to build a personal AI Safe Use Playbook. Newly published (6 students).

courses.title: AI Security Bootcamp-Guardrails,LLM Gateways,Observability

Coding-along throughout.

courses.title: AI Security Bridge Course | CISSP, SSCP, CGRC, CCSP & CSSLP
courses.description: Lecture-only course (Cyvitrix) mapping ISC2 AI security guidance onto five certifications: a shared foundation (governance, asset classification, data lifecycle, secure architecture, access control for models/agents/APIs, AI gateways, adversarial attacks, assurance and impact assessments, privacy, incident response, monitoring, lineage), then per-certification deltas on regulation, prompt monitoring, AI risk assessment and controls, supply chain and vendor risk, guardrail testing, RAG, AI dev tools and MITRE ATLAS. No labs, quizzes or practice tests.

courses.title: AI Security Engineer Bootcamp
courses.description: Introductory AI security engineering course: AI/ML basics (tokens, embeddings, models), the AI security engineer role, model, data and system security (backend, frontend, MCP/middleware, governance), then a 1-hour guided case study threat-modelling an agentic AI system with CSA's MAESTRO (data-flow diagram, manual and automated threat identification, final report). One knowledge check.

courses.title: AI Security Essentials
courses.description: Lecture course on securing AI/ML systems in a few long modules: AI security concepts and frameworks, model and dataset threats (poisoning, evasion, inversion, adversarial attacks), AI infrastructure security and incident response, anomaly detection and threat intelligence, and ethics/privacy-preserving ML and a regulatory overview. Self-assessed assignments (threat modelling and mitigation plan, IR plan) and a bonus on building a custom GPT; no agent content.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N4 Weak 11%; N5 Weak 11%; N12 Weak 11%; N13 Weak 6% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.

courses.title: AI Security: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic AI Systems
courses.description: Walks through all ten OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications risks (ASI01 goal hijack to ASI10 rogue agents), each with an overview, two or three enterprise scenarios (refunds, payments, DevOps, trading, wire transfers), a technology map and a shared defence architecture (trust boundaries, bounded execution, task-scoped identity, provenance and pinning, sandboxing, memory write controls, mTLS/signatures between agents, circuit breakers, drift detection and kill switches). Ten knowledge-check quizzes and a final assessment; no hands-on labs.

courses.title: AI Strategy for Business: Identify and Evaluate Use Cases
courses.description: Business-oriented course on finding and qualifying AI use cases: AI solution types, spotting pain points, a value/feasibility/risk evaluation framework, writing requirements for the AI team, a pilot-to-deployment roadmap with business KPIs, three scenario workshops (marketing, operations, finance), two practice tests and a role play. Not cyber-specific and nothing on agents.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence Governance Professional (AIGP)
courses.description: Exam-prep course for IAPP AIGP (Body of Knowledge v2.1) in 115 lectures: AI foundations, harms and responsible-AI principles, governance structures and risk tiering with NIST AI RMF, governing development (impact assessments, data governance, model cards), governing deployment (third-party risk, drift, incident response, auditing, RAG, agentic AI), the EU AI Act in depth and other laws and ISO 42001/42005. Includes scenario activities, section assessments, two practice tests and a governance-roadmap activity.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk and Cyber Security Course 2026
courses.description: Awareness course in 17 lectures (no labs, three knowledge-check quizzes): AI/ML overview, AI governance, bias, regulations (OECD, EU AI Act, ISO 42001) and NIST AI RMF, AI-specific attacks (poisoning, evasion, extraction, membership inference), AI security testing with MITRE ATLAS and tools named, agentic AI and its risks, and the AWS Generative AI and Agentic AI Security Scoping Matrices.

courses.title: Change Management in the GenAI Era: Adoption & Governance
courses.description: 13 lectures with four section knowledge checks, four scenario items (CFO buy-in for a pilot, negotiating guardrails, union concerns, stopping risky public AI use) and a final challenge. courses.title: CompTIA SecAI+ 2026: Complete AI Security Exam Prep
courses.description: Slide-based exam prep for CompTIA SecAI+ (CY0-001): about 40 lectures of roughly 3 minutes on AI fundamentals, lifecycle and data security, the AI threat landscape, OWASP LLM risks, MITRE ATLAS and threat-modelling scenarios, identity, guardrails, logging, AI in the SOC, and governance. Includes eight module quizzes, scenario items and two 45-question practice tests; no labs.

courses.title: Critical Thinking with AI & GenAI Fundamentals!!
courses.description: Conceptual, tool-free course whose core (Sec 3, 15 lectures, about 1.5h) covers critical thinking, how AI thinks, cognitive biases in humans and AI, questioning AI outputs, decision-making with AI input, problem framing and mental frameworks. The other ~65 hours are 'additional training resources' bundled from unrelated topics (SAP, Six Sigma, TOGAF, GCFE, sales, personal branding, AI cybersecurity). No exercises or quizzes.

courses.title: Data Governance & AI Governance: The Complete Guide
courses.description: Dr. Florian Detzel's two-part programme: roughly two-thirds classic data governance (operating model, policies and controls, catalog, data quality, privacy, lineage), then AI governance modules on fundamentals, responsible AI (risk taxonomy, scoring, impact assessment, model cards, risk register), ML lifecycle (model registry, approval gates), GenAI/LLM governance (RAG corpora, prompt and output controls, logging, acceptance criteria), AI data quality and drift, AI incident runbooks and governance tooling. Every module has a template-based exercise on a car-rental case study (EasyCar) with a sample solution; the Coursera/Packt edition lists 15 assignments and a final assessment. Frameworks referenced: EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, GDPR.

courses.title: Data Governance in the Age of AI
courses.description: Short overview by Georgi Smarts of how AI changes data governance: training-data quality, a bias case study, AI and privacy (GDPR/CCPA), a policy template and RACI, a five-minute tour of AI regulations (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF), and downloadable templates (AI data risk matrix, ethics guidelines, model documentation, compliance checklist). Lectures are 3-7 minutes each; one optional Udemy lab to fill in an AI model governance card.

courses.title: Developing a Security and Compliance Program with GenAI
courses.description: Rassoul Zadeh walks beginners through building an ISO 27001 / NIST CSF assessment programme (planning, assessment interviews, remediation, monitoring) using ChatGPT or Bard to generate questionnaires, interview questions and responses. It is demonstration-based, with no labs or quizzes, and opens with a 'General Warning' lecture.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N1 Partial 33%; N6 Weak 21%; R6.1 Weak 17% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Use of AI to draft control-assessment material is shown; systematic validation/monitoring of that assessment AI is not taught. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: EU AI Act Compliance Introduction
courses.description: Robert Barcik and Jana Gecelovská go article by article through the EU AI Act: definitions (including autonomy), the Article 4 staff-training duty, prohibited practices, high-risk classification and Annex III, provider requirements (Art 9-15: risk management, data, documentation, record keeping, human oversight, accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity), transparency and deepfake duties, GPAI, enforcement and sandboxes. It is kept current (2026 Digital Omnibus, fines, ISO 42001 vs the Act), with knowledge quizzes per Title and no practical exercises.

courses.title: EU AI Act Compliance: High-Risk, GPAI and Governance
courses.description: DCDG Partners' compact, current (post-2026 Omnibus) EU AI Act course: scope and roles, the ten prohibitions, high-risk classification via Annex I/III and the Art 6(3) filter, provider and deployer obligations, Article 50 transparency, GPAI and what to demand from model vendors, enforcement, and building a compliance programme (inventory, triage, governance, monitoring, 90-day plan). N5.8.evidence: V11 reassessment (18 October 2026). Security/privacy risks, safety constraints or controls are named in the retained public syllabus, but a coherent explanation of the revised security-risk overview is not established. Reviewed syllabus: DCDG Partners' compact, current (post-2026 Omnibus) EU AI Act course: scope and roles, the ten prohibitions, high-risk classification via Annex I/III and the Art 6(3) filter, provider and deployer obligations, Article 50 transparency, GPAI and what to demand from model vendors, enforcement, and building a compliance programme (inventory, triage, governance, monitoring, 90-day plan). It comes with downloadable kits (Excel classification engine, FRIA template, vendor questionnaire, inventory workbook) but no graded exercises.

courses.title: EU AI Act Masterclass: Compliance, Risk & Governance 2026
courses.description: Pavan Kumar and Manish Patel cover the EU AI Act in about 134 one-minute lectures: scope, risk tiers, high-risk compliance (data governance, documentation, logging, human oversight, robustness), GPAI, sector rules including finance, enforcement, compliance preparation and technical/organisational measures. Each section ends with scenario 'workshops' and simulations (e.g. human oversight gap review, CE documentation review) and a quiz; 6 of 16 sections were not visible.

courses.title: Evaluation for LLM Applications
courses.description: A one-hour survey of LLM evaluation: intrinsic vs extrinsic evals, observability and logging, failure categorisation and root cause, human vs automatic evaluation and LLM-as-a-judge, RAG retrieval metrics, evaluation in CI/CD and production alerting, human review and cost. Each topic gets a 2-3 minute lecture and a section quiz; there are no notebooks or hands-on exercises.

courses.title: Gen AI Literacy for Employees and Managers
courses.description: Vasco Patrício's single-module literacy course: where GenAI stands, what it can actually do, how it changes work and workflows, technical basics (parameters, context, training, fine-tuning, hallucinations), common adoption pain points (output quality, workflow fit), and his AHEADS model. Long lecture blocks of 17-30 minutes plus a role-play on teaching GenAI literacy; no quizzes or labs.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N1 Partial 44%; N3 Weak 10%; N6 Weak 21%; N14 Weak 10% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.

courses.title: GenAI Cybersecurity Solutions: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Apps
courses.description: Start-Tech Academy walks through the original (2023) OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications: prompt injection (direct and indirect), insecure output handling, supply chain, model DoS, training data poisoning, sensitive information disclosure and plugin security; per the description, excessive agency, overreliance and model theft sit in 3 sections not visible on the page. It includes lab-based demos on PortSwigger Web Security Academy (indirect prompt injection, insecure output handling; four exercises announced), short quizzes and an interview role-play.

courses.title: GenAI Fundamentals for UX Designers + Researchers
courses.description: Joe Natoli teaches UX and product designers how to design GenAI features: when AI is appropriate, automation vs assistance, reward functions and precision/recall trade-offs, designing for variability, imperfect outputs, confidence scores, controls, explanation and trust, and designing against harms (misuse, deepfakes) with value-sensitive design. Lectures plus a 164-page workbook with 89 exercises.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N3 Weak 10%; N14 Weak 5%; R5.1 Weak 11% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): UX lessons explicitly address confidence displays, user controls and friction to prevent over-reliance. Transferable to approval-interface design but incomplete for agents/banking. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: Generative AI - Risk and Cyber Security Masterclass 2026
courses.description: Taimur Ijlal (a former CISO) gives security and risk professionals an overview of GenAI risk: LLM basics and GenAI vs agentic AI (with a role-play CIO meeting), then data privacy and confidentiality, provider breach, threat actors, data leakage, direct and indirect prompt injection (with a sandbox demo), inadequate sandboxing, hallucinations, SSRF, DDoS, data poisoning, bias and copyright, and how to secure GenAI (threat modelling, a governance checklist, the AWS GenAI Security Scoping Matrix, OWASP Top 10 for LLMs 2025). It is lecture-led with one demo and no labs or quizzes.

courses.title: Generative AI for Leaders: Strategy & Innovation
courses.description: Mana Dowlatshahi Yeganeh course whose core is 39 six-minute lectures (Dec 2025) on business strategy, marketing, management and GenAI, one lecture each on ethics/risk and AI policy, plus a previous version and an AI-fundamentals block (LLMs, image/video, speech AI). About 140 hours are 'bonus' material repackaged from other courses (SD-WAN, TOGAF, Six Sigma, SAP, and long lectures titled 'AI-Driven SOC Fundamentals', 'AI Agents for Cybersecurity', 'Securing GenAI Systems'); no labs.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N1 Partial 33%; N2 Weak 14%; N4 Weak 6%; N6 Weak 4%; N14 Weak 10% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.

courses.title: Generative AI Risks & Cybersecurity: LLM Security
courses.description: Dr. Amar Massoud course on GenAI security with 14 labs against a local Llama 3.2 model: threat landscape and provider breaches, hallucination probing, direct and indirect prompt injection with data exfiltration, jailbreaking, data poisoning, bias, SSRF and DoS, then defences (defence-in-depth, input validation, guardrails builder, output validation, sandboxing, monitoring with an incident-response simulator), secure development, vendor evaluation, red teaming, regulation, audits, IP, and agentic attack surfaces; quizzes per section and a capstone red-team lab.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N2 Weak 24%; N3 Partial 48%; N4 Partial 57%; N5 Partial 39%; N9 Weak 13%; N11 Weak 11%; N12 Partial 41%; N13 Partial 33%; N14 Weak 5%; R3.1 Partial 50%; R6.1 Weak 17% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Attack/defence labs supply security checks, and agent lecture names per-tool boundaries. Generic LLM incident simulation is not agent incident-response training. Context-window exhaustion is explained alongside token processing and attacks. Temperature is named as affecting safety, without full non-determinism teaching. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: Hallucination Management for Generative AI
courses.description: Atil Samancioglu course on LLM hallucinations: causes, hands-on experiments across GPT-4, Gemini and Llama, temperature and sampling in the OpenAI Playground, mitigation by prompt revision, grounding, chain of verification and step-back prompting (LangChain code), RAG with a hallucination grader, fine-tuning comparisons, and LLM vulnerability scanning and hallucination detection tools. Code demos with GitHub material.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N2 Weak 5%; N3 Partial 43%; N6 Weak 21%; N9 Weak 27%; N11 Weak 11%; R3.1 Weak 13% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Hallucination grader and scanner examples provide evaluation checks and automated testing. Judge presence does not evidence validation against human labels. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: Hands On AI (LLM) Red Teaming
courses.description: Jitendra Chauhan (Detoxio AI) course with a provided lab VM: running local models (Ollama, Hugging Face), adversarial ML testing with IBM ART and TextAttack, AI attack taxonomy and data poisoning (PoisonGPT), Garak scans, a 3-hour prompt-injection/jailbreak block with hands-on targets (Text2SqlAgent, PokeBot, Medusa) and a 1-hour OWASP Top 10 for LLM Apps lecture, reasoning models and AI agents (autonomous pentesting agent demo, building an AutoGen agent), and mitigations with Prompt Guard and Llama Guard.

courses.title: Haystack-Build and Evaluate Agentic Generative AI Pipelines
courses.description: Developer course on the Haystack 2.0 framework: pipelines, components, document stores, retrievers, RAG (including an AWS Bedrock Knowledge Base bonus), prompt building, and RAG evaluation with Haystack evaluators and RAGAS (LLM-as-judge faithfulness, SAS, context relevance). Advanced section covers hybrid retrieval, rerankers, self-correcting loops and agentic pipelines built with OpenAI function calling. Delivered as video lectures with hands-on Python coding walkthroughs; one of 11 sections was collapsed on the page.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N6 Weak 8%; N9 Weak 20%; N10 Weak 21%; N11 Weak 11% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Prompt construction and model-based RAG evaluators add partial personal context/evaluation awareness; no judge calibration. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: Human Judgment in the Age of AI & Algorithms
courses.description: Short course (Anton Voroniuk; the page says it contains AI-generated content) on evaluating AI outputs with human judgment: cognitive, algorithmic and automation bias, why confident answers can be wrong, checking evidence and sources, defining the decision before consulting AI, and taking responsibility. Four short 'Practice' scenario lectures (identify bias, evaluate an AI-supported decision, apply a human-in-the-loop framework, respond to an ethical scenario); no labs.

courses.description: Leadership-oriented course (GenMan Solutions) on deciding what to delegate to AI, directing it, evaluating its outputs and redesigning team work. Built around an AI delegation test, a four-level delegation framework and case studies (Amazon recruiting, Air Canada, Uber surge pricing, the lawyer with fabricated cases, Zillow, Netflix, Klarna). Includes reflection activities, delegation assessments and a personal action plan; no labs.

courses.description: Three modules (Vasco Patrício): Gen AI literacy (what Gen AI can do, how it changes work, technical aspects, common pain points), a structured method for judging Gen AI outputs (validation process plus assumption, grounding, consistency, specificity/capability and negative-evidence 'sweeps'), and role, organisational, mindset and cognitive transformation. Long lectures with one role-play; no labs or graded exercises.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N1 Partial 44%; N3 Partial 38%; N6 Weak 12%; N14 Weak 29% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Current transformation lectures explain execution/orchestration changes and cognitive degradation; no protected junior-pipeline programme. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: Human-centered AI for Leaders
courses.description: Academic-style course on human-centred AI design for leaders: human psychology, human-in-the-loop vs human-on-the-loop, trustworthy and explainable interfaces, AI for creativity, emotional support and wellbeing, data dignity, evaluation beyond accuracy, prototyping and an impact lifecycle map. Lectures with reflective prompts and a capstone; no labs.

courses.title: Hybrid Teams: Leading Human-AI Collaboration
courses.description: Short course (Data Universe) on leading teams of people and AI agents: shared roles, collaboration models, task allocation, KPIs and joint evaluation of human and AI contributions, change resistance, skills gaps, ethics, privacy and regulation. 29 lectures of about 3 minutes each, ending with three case studies; no labs.

courses.title: IAPP AIGP Certification: 2026 AI Governance Exam Prep
courses.description: Large exam-prep course (Sachin Aggarwal, 295 short lectures) mapped to the IAPP AIGP body of knowledge: AI foundations and inherent risks (hallucination, drift, automation bias, prompt injection, poisoning, extraction), OECD/NIST AI RMF/ISO 42001/ISO 23894, EU AI Act, GDPR and other laws, lifecycle governance (inventories, TPRM, vendor due diligence, TEVV, HITL/HOTL, red teaming), deployment and monitoring (drift, incidents, kill switch, logs, audits), strategy and culture (AUP, shadow AI, agentic workflows) and sector cases. Section quizzes and three practice exams; no hands-on labs.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N2 Partial 33%; N3 Partial 48%; N4 Partial 48%; N5 Partial 33%; N7 Weak 7%; N9 Weak 7%; N11 Weak 28%; N12 Weak 7%; N13 Partial 61%; N14 Weak 14%; R3.1 Weak 17% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.

Security/privacy risks, safety constraints or controls are named in the retained public syllabus, but a coherent explanation of the revised security-risk overview is not established. Reviewed syllabus: One-module foundation (Vasco Patrício): what AI is, discriminative vs generative AI, AI issues and risks, responsible AI principles (fairness, transparency, accountability, data protection), governance and risk management basics, and the regulatory landscape (EU AI Act, GDPR, NIST AI RMF). Three quizzes and four short browser 'simulator' labs (fairness control, launch, accountability, system design).

courses.title: ISO 42001 - AI Management System - Lead Implementer Course
courses.description: Clause-by-clause walkthrough of ISO/IEC 42001 (Hemang Doshi): context, leadership, planning incl. AI risk assessment, treatment and impact assessment (6.1.2-6.1.4), support, operations, performance evaluation, improvement and Annex A controls, ending with an implementation guide and interview prep. Each clause has a video and a text version, with practice questions and downloadable policy and assessment templates; no labs.

courses.title: ISO 42001 AIMS: AI Management System Guide
courses.description: Guide (Fortivance Academy) to understanding, implementing and auditing ISO/IEC 42001:2023: AI governance landscape, clause structure, AI policies and organisation, impact assessments and risk integration, lifecycle management, data management, stakeholder transparency, operations and incident management, and third-party and supply-chain risk. Knowledge checks, short case items and a downloadable toolkit (policies, risk register, impact assessment, RACI, incident response templates); only 10 of 19 sections were visible.

courses.title: ISO 42001:2023 - AI Management System Lead Mastery Course
courses.description: ISO/IEC 42001 course (Cyvitrix Learning, text-to-speech narration) covering clauses 4-9, AI risk assessment, treatment and impact assessment, AI threats (data integrity and adversarial attacks), threat modelling, shadow AI, third-party AI procurement and supply-chain assurance, AI incident response, human oversight models, logging requirements, auditing and bias monitoring, mapped to ISO 27001/31000 and the NIST AI RMF. Section quizzes and 21 templates; only 10 of 16 sections were visible; no labs.

courses.title: LLM Applications: Prototyping, and Evaluation
courses.description: Short code-along on evaluating a RAG 'chat with your data' application: RAGAS metrics (context precision, context recall, faithfulness), building an evaluation dataset, LangSmith tracing and experiments, and running the evaluation on AWS. The lectures are hands-on code walkthroughs with source code. There are no graded exercises.

courses.title: LLM Observability and Cost Management: Langfuse, Monitoring
courses.description: Developer course on instrumenting LLM applications with Langfuse: the cost drivers of LLM apps (tokens, RAG and agent pipelines), Langfuse setup and data model, and hands-on instrumentation of a multi-step RAG pipeline and LangChain. It also covers cost optimisation (prompt trimming, semantic caching, model routing), alerting, and a short section on security and compliance patterns such as PII redaction. It has code demos but no graded labs.

courses.title: Mastering the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
courses.description: Walks through the 2023 (v1.1) OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, one demo and one quiz per risk. The demos include prompt injection with Kali and Gandalf, a PortSwigger insecure-output lab, data poisoning, model DoS, typosquatting supply chain, sensitive information disclosure, insecure plugin design, excessive agency and overreliance. One final section is not listed on the page.

courses.title: MCP: Model Context Protocol for AI Governance & Security
courses.description: No-code course on the Model Context Protocol for governance, security and compliance professionals. It covers roles and session model, primitives (tools, resources, prompts, sampling, roots), the security model (consent, credentials, allowlists, OAuth 2.1/PKCE), prompt injection via tool descriptions, forbidden patterns and server vetting. Later sections compare MCP with A2A and function calling and cover enterprise gateways, registries, auditing MCP traffic, and the EU AI Act, ISO 42001 and NIST AI RMF. Assessment is two practice tests and a role play; there are no hands-on labs.

courses.title: Microsoft Security Copilot Hands On Course with Simulations
courses.description: Hands-on product course on Microsoft Security Copilot in a trial M365/Azure tenant. It covers Defender, Sentinel and Purview basics, SCU allocation, roles, prompts and promptbooks, incident investigation with prompts and promptbooks, script and Entra ID analysis, DLP guidance, and Microsoft and custom plugins (Shodan, CIRCL). Learners work through instructor-led simulations; the last two sections are not listed on the page.

courses.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework (RMF) Masterclass - 2026
courses.description: Structured walk-through of the NIST AI RMF: AI risks and incidents, the framework's foundation and trustworthy-AI characteristics, then every GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE and MANAGE category. It closes with lectures on combining the RMF with other frameworks and extending it to agentic AI risks. There are seven knowledge checks and illustrative case studies, but no hands-on assessment exercise.

courses.title: Organizational Redesign in the AI Era
courses.description: Short, partly AI-generated course (Anton Voroniuk) on redesigning structures, roles and workflows for AI. It covers readiness assessment, task classification (automate, augment, keep human), workflow mapping, team structures, change and resistance, and reskilling. Learning is through four business cases (support, operations, knowledge work, sales), templates, an interactive role play and a self-directed capstone redesign plan.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N1 Weak 11%; N6 Weak 4%; N14 Partial 38% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Task sorting/workforce scenarios introduce individual work change and delegation alongside existing organisational redesign scores. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: Organizational Redesign in the AI Era
courses.description: Course (GenMan Solutions) for leaders and transformation staff on how organisations should change when AI joins the workforce. It covers structure, decisions, workflow and culture, workforce impact by level, and the Keep/Change/Remove framework for tasks. Further topics are readiness, the cost-benefit case, a metrics dashboard, presenting to executives, and risk, security, privacy and compliance. Exercises include a graded-by-answer-key task sort, a spreadsheet metrics dashboard on a claims-processing scenario, role plays and a 90-day/12-month roadmap workbook.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N4 Weak 5%; N13 Weak 6%; N14 Partial 52% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Risk/privacy section introduces organisational AI safeguards; no technical agent security inferred from business supply-chain use cases. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: Penetration Testing for LLMs
courses.description: Introductory course on pentesting LLM applications. It covers GenAI basics, pentest methodology and a GenAI pentest process, MITRE ATT&CK (49 min) and MITRE ATLAS with case studies, and the 2025 OWASP LLM Top 10. It ends with a demo case study on PortSwigger's LLM labs (indirect prompt injection, insecure output handling, supply chain, excessive agency). The demos are instructor-led, though learners can replicate the free labs.

N5.8.evidence: V11 reassessment (18 October 2026). The reviewed syllabus teaches selected attack/risk families or precautions. Coverage of all six families with examples and a precaution/escalation response is not evidenced. No full overview credit is inferred from a framework name or a narrow lab. Reviewed syllabus: Introductory course on pentesting LLM applications. It covers GenAI basics, pentest methodology and a GenAI pentest process, MITRE ATT&CK (49 min) and MITRE ATLAS with case studies, and the 2025 OWASP LLM Top 10. It ends with a demo case study on PortSwigger's LLM labs (indirect prompt injection, insecure output handling, supply chain, excessive agency). The demos are instructor-led, though learners can replicate the free labs.

courses.title: Practical GenAI: Basics, Tools, Use cases, Ethics, Future
courses.description: Broad productivity course for business employees: tool walkthroughs (ChatGPT, Bard, Claude 2, Midjourney, Runway, ElevenLabs and others), a prompt-engineering section on six strategies with a quiz, and many use cases (marketing content, business tasks, job hunting, SQL/Python/HTML with ChatGPT, a RAG masterclass, SEO). Six of the 16 sections were not visible on the page. Ethics is only touched, and limitations such as hallucination or data privacy were not evidenced.

courses.title: Responsible AI in Business: Ethics, Risk & Compliance

Lectures plus three scenario exercises (explain an AI denial, negotiate job-impact guardrails, coach a colleague after a data-handling slip), knowledge checks and a final challenge.

courses.title: Responsible AI: A Non-Technical Guide for Managers

courses.title: Responsible AI. Principles, Risks and Professional Practice
courses.description: Judgment-focused course for professionals using AI: how AI 'thinks', bias, why AI makes things up and how to verify it, privacy (prompts as business information, using public AI tools with confidential information), adversarial inputs, human-in-the-loop and override, what can and cannot be delegated, disclosure, organisational AI policy (ISO/IEC 42001) and automation bias. Lectures only; 2 of 12 sections were collapsed on the page and no exercises or quizzes are listed.

courses.title: SC-500: Microsoft Cloud and AI Security Engineer Exam Prep
courses.description: Lab-driven SC-500 exam prep (about 100 hands-on labs, GitHub repo, two practice tests) covering Entra, Purview (incl. DSPM for AI), Key Vault, storage, SQL, networking, compute, Sentinel and Security Copilot. A dedicated section 'Implement Security for AI Agents and Applications' has labs on Entra Agent ID, Conditional Access for agents, Agent 365 policy templates, Global Secure Access baselines for agents, Defender integration, Foundry AI Gateway and rate limiting, agent evaluation and monitoring, and Foundry guardrails.

courses.title: The AI Ethics Course 2026: Work with AI Responsibly
courses.description: 365 Careers course on AI ethics across the lifecycle: core principles, ethical data collection and model development (labelled data, fine-tuning, RLHF), deployment issues (IP, inconsistency, hallucination, monitoring), business and individual use, ChatGPT ethics (privacy, OpenAI data handling, plagiarism) and regulatory frameworks (GDPR, EU AI Act, US, APAC). Short lectures with case examples; no quizzes or exercises listed.

courses.title: The EU AI Act Compliance Masterclass 2026
courses.description: Short video course by Taimur Ijlal on the EU AI Act: an overview of AI and of the Act, the risk tiers (minimal, unacceptable, high risk with a case study), general-purpose AI with a case study, a compliance process flow, and two short lectures on governance and implementing the Act. Lectures only: no quizzes, exercises or labs are listed. It does not cover APAC regulators, the bank's own rules or anything specific to agents.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: Historical pre-v11 snapshot: N4 Weak 11%; N13 Partial 39% | Current v11 results: Coverage sheet.
courses.limitations: V8 (15 Oct 2026): Published compliance process and high-risk case include model inventory, risk triage and obligations-to-controls. Lack of APAC coverage limits, rather than eliminates, N13. Prior fit note retained in V8 audit.

courses.title: Total:AI Risk Management for Security Managers
courses.description: Unofficial ISACA AAISM exam-prep course by Dr. Michael Solomon (Total Seminars), in 47 video lectures across 6 sections plus 6 chapter quizzes (106 knowledge-check questions). It covers AI governance (steering committee, risk appetite, policy, inventory), AI risk assessment and treatment, EU AI Act provider and deployer status, vendor and 3rd/4th/5th-party risk, threats (MITRE ATLAS, OWASP LLM Top 10, red teaming, deepfakes, data poisoning), AI incident response with red-button and break-glass controls, resilience, and control selection and monitoring. It has no labs or exercises, is aimed at security managers holding CISM or CISSP, and covers agents in only one lecture.

courses.title: Ultimate IAPP AIGP Masterclass - Lead AI Governance
courses.description: Long, unofficial IAPP AIGP exam-prep course by Cyvitrix Learning, in 130 lectures across 16 sections. It covers AI foundations, responsible AI and harms, governance programme design (operating model, RACI, inventory, intake), AI risk management and control assurance, AI law and regulation (AI Act-style risk classification, privacy, IP, liability), NIST AI RMF and ISO 42001/42005, governing development, data and testing, deployment (including vendor AI and agentic deployment), incidents, drift, and audit and assurance. Practice comes from 20+ quizzes, six case studies (one on agentic workflow automation), domain reviews and a capstone 'Build an AI Governance Pack'. The content of the final section was only partly visible, and there are no labs.

N5.8.evidence: V11 reassessment (18 October 2026). Security/privacy risks, safety constraints or controls are named in the retained public syllabus, but a coherent explanation of the revised security-risk overview is not established. Reviewed syllabus: Long, unofficial IAPP AIGP exam-prep course by Cyvitrix Learning, in 130 lectures across 16 sections. It covers AI foundations, responsible AI and harms, governance programme design (operating model, RACI, inventory, intake), AI risk management and control assurance, AI law and regulation (AI Act-style risk classification, privacy, IP, liability), NIST AI RMF and ISO 42001/42005, governing development, data and testing, deployment (including vendor AI and agentic deployment), incidents, drift, and audit and assurance. Practice comes from 20+ quizzes, six case studies (one on agentic workflow automation), domain reviews and a capstone 'Build an AI Governance Pack'. The content of the final section was only partly visible, and there are no labs.

courses.description: AI foundations, prompting and redaction, secure lifecycle, threat modelling, guardrails and gateways, IAM, monitoring, attack evidence and compensating controls, AI security use cases, low/no-code automation, change approval/rollback, agents/MCP and GRC.
courses.coverageAtAssessment: All 140 active outcomes assessed independently on the unchanged 0–3 rubric. See Coverage for scoped results and Scores for outcome-specific evidence.
courses.limitations: Public curriculum assessment only; purchased lessons and learner submissions not inspected. Animated/interactive video lessons and two domain-weighted practice exams with explanations. Interactive presentation is not verified hands-on learner practice. Bank policy, complete agent supervision, reusable Skills and evaluation need additional learning. Full listed video duration applies; tests, role plays and assignments may take additional unquantified time. Subscription inclusion unverified. courses.coverageAtAssessment: All 140 active outcomes assessed independently on the unchanged 0–3 rubric. See Coverage for scoped results and Scores for outcome-specific evidence.
courses.limitations: Public curriculum assessment only; purchased lessons and learner submissions not inspected. 17 demonstrations advertised across the four modules, including data minimisation, model poisoning, incident summaries and authority mapping. Full listed video duration applies; tests, role plays and assignments may take additional unquantified time. Subscription inclusion unverified. Ratings select the shortlist; they do not create coverage or prove quality.

scoringGuide: All Offers are reviewed against active outcomes. V11 preserves the 0–3 rubric and band thresholds. Knowledge needs require suitable depth; skill needs require practice for score 3. Retired outcomes are excluded from active calculations.
No teaching or mention evidenced in the reviewed course synopsis/source. This is not a claim that no such training exists.
Named or touched on, but not taught: a learner could not explain or apply it afterwards.
Explained in enough depth to understand it, but covers only part of what the requirement lists, or has no practice where the need is a skill.

Covers everything the requirement lists in enough depth to apply it. For skill needs (N6 to N14 and the role extras) learners practise it in an exercise, lab or realistic case. For knowledge needs (N1 to N5) depth and completeness are enough.
Coverage needed for Strong, provided no must-have (Core) requirement scores 0.
Coverage needed for Partial. Below it the band is Weak.
Coverage at or above the Strong minimum, and no Core requirement at 0. A course above the minimum but missing a Core requirement drops to Partial.
Coverage at or above the Partial minimum.
The need's active requirements at or below the level the training targets. An Expert course on N4 is scored on N4.1 to N4.7; a Base course on N4.1 to N4.6.
Sum of the scores of the in-scope requirements, divided by 3 times their number. A requirement not yet scored counts as 0.
A must-have requirement: without it the need is not met, whatever the coverage. The Core flags in the Rubric are a first proposal, one to three per need, to be confirmed by the domain heads.

A must-have is essential to achieving the objective safely and effectively at the assigned depth. Conditional essentials are identified in Rubric Notes. Strong requires no applicable must-have at zero; a mention can clear that gate but does not establish competence.

Two to five trainings combined to cover a need. A path takes, for each requirement, the best score any of its trainings achieved. Requirements still below 3 in the best path are the build list for that need.

rows: A training that showcases what AI does today in cyber by showing existing use in our organization, discuss about planned future development and beyond.

N1.1 · What AI does today in cyber
Describe what AI and agents already do well in one's own domain and the neighbouring ones: triage and enrichment, log and code analysis, drafting and summarising, policy mapping, test generation

N1.2 · What is emerging
Describe what is emerging in AI for cyber, beyond what is in production today

N1.3 · How one's own work changes
Name two or three ways one's own work could change. The purpose is to open the mind to a new way of working, not to teach a tool
